why: Each process adds 1 to every minute in [start, end]; the answer is the highest point of that running total. That is a sweep line (difference array over events) with inclusive ends, the same max-overlap idea as the intervals chapter.
hints: Picture adding +1 for every minute a process is alive. Where does the total peak?
Turn each log into two events: +1 at startTime and -1 at endTime + 1 (the first minute it is no longer running). Sort events and keep a running sum.
Sort the 2n events by time (a -1 at time t sorts before a +1 at t, which is fine since the -1 means 'stopped before t'). Track the maximum running sum. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Inclusive end: [1,3] and [3,6] are both running at minute 3. Put the -1 at end + 1, not at end.
A one-minute process [5,5] still counts at minute 5.
constraints:
• 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5 (not stated in the source)
  • 0 ≤ startTime ≤ endTime ≤ 10^9 (not stated in the source)
  • Both endpoints are inclusive.
